what_its_for: Alfuzosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate gland (also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH) in men. It helps relax the muscles in your prostate and bladder, making it easier for you to urinate. Common symptoms it helps with include a weak urine stream, trouble starting to urinate, needing to go frequently, or waking up at night to use the bathroom.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or break the tablet. Always take it with a meal, at the same time each day — right after breakfast or your largest meal of the day works well. Taking it with food helps your body absorb the medicine properly and lowers the chance of dizziness.
dosing: The usual dose for adults is one 10 mg extended-release tablet taken by mouth once a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Do not take more than one tablet per day.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day and you have eaten a meal. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store alfuzosin at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in your bathroom medicine cabinet. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired tablets safely — check with your pharmacist about local medication take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, especially when you first start this medicine — this can cause dizziness or fainting due to a sudden drop in blood pressure. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking alfuzosin, as it can increase the risk of dizziness and low blood pressure. Tell your dentist, eye doctor, and all healthcare providers that you take alfuzosin before any surgery or procedure, especially eye surgery for cataracts.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: a sudden drop in blood pressure causing dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting; chest pain or irregular heartbeat; a painful or prolonged erection lasting more than 4 hours (priapism) — this is a medical emergency; severe allergic reaction signs such as rash, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing; or if your urinary symptoms do not improve or get worse.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your urinary symptoms within 1 to 2 weeks of starting alfuzosin. However, it may take up to 4 to 6 weeks to feel the full benefit. Keep taking it as directed even if you feel better, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: This medicine is only for use in adult men. It should NOT be used in women or children. Men with severe liver problems should not take alfuzosin. If you have kidney problems, heart disease, low blood pressure, or a history of QT prolongation (a heart rhythm problem), tell your doctor before starting this medicine. Also tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, and supplements, as alfuzosin can interact with several medications, especially other blood pressure medicines and certain antibiotics or antifungals.
